editorial:
Imagine sitting across from one of the most hated men in America, trying to get him to admit to a crime that shocked the whole country. You get to follow a reporter who is on a mission to crack the case of Alex Murdaugh, the powerful lawyer accused of killing his own wife and son. The vibe is tense and focused, feeling less like a big action movie and more like a high-stakes game of chess. You spend most of the time watching the battle of wills between the journalist and the prisoner, wondering if you can actually trust a single word coming out of Murdaugh's mouth.

What really works here is the acting, as the lead does a great job of playing a guy who thinks he is the smartest person in the room. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the psychological tension keeps you glued to your seat. If you love true crime podcasts or documentaries, you will definitely enjoy this. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the facial expressions, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing the breakdown of Murdaugh's lies. As the reporter keeps digging and asking the right questions, the cracks in his story become too big to hide. You see the final pieces of evidence fall into place, proving that his image as a family man was a total lie. He ends up facing the consequences of his crimes, leaving you with a feeling of justice served after a long, messy legal battle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime stories and courtroom dramas.
